content.text:
I made the http adapter's content-encoding check case-insensitive, so responses marked `GZIP`, `Gzip`, `Deflate`, `BR` and so on are now decompressed. I haven't run any tests or written a new one for it.

The fix is a one-line change in `lib/adapters/http.js:474`. The adapter compares the header against `gzip`, `x-gzip`, `compress`, `x-compress`, `deflate` and `br`, and now lowercases the value before that comparison.

For HEAD and 204 responses the code removes the header just before this check. In that case the value falls back to an empty string, so it neither crashes nor tries to decompress.
